posts.name: Phantom5613
posts.cooked:
As I'm sure you guys have seen, a new KS update came out! Here's where you can give it a read: https://www.kickstarter.com/projects/gtgames/sentinels-of-the-multiverse-oblivaeon/posts/1862354

And with this we've had a glimpse at each new OblivAeon hero! I like the idea of Benchmark and of how 'technological' his powerset is shown to be. Without looking at any of his other cards I'm going to say he's a 1-2 difficulty hero, depending on what cards of his you decide to focus on.

It looks like we really are gonna see Stuntman's personality through his deck, him being all about out-of-turn actions and such to 'show other heroes up'. I find that kind of funny/annoying, but that's the whole point, isn't it?

And of course we get a shout out for Sentinels of Earth-Prime(which I totally backed already, and you should check out if you haven't), which happily funded on its first day.

And it looks like we're gonna get a look at our five new environments next time, along with an update about the collector's box! Can't wait for May!

posts.name: Jeysie
posts.cooked:
I feel like Stuntman is like an Insufferable Genius version of Gambit, which I consider to be a very good and amusing thing. He's in that kind of fun dynamic where he has an annoying ego the size of a planet but actually can be good enough at times to justify it.

I like the look of Benchmark too; the build-a-hero flavor to his cards are interesting, and I like that we'll be getting to meet an actual unique hero (as in not a good or evil twin) from an alternate universe who will therefore have a different culture to work from. Especially one that's still strongly tied to Revo-Corp so we get to see more from them as well.

I thought it was Revenant's suit, being repurposed as a hero suit as Revocorp tries to pull some shenanigans.

Benchmark isn't super comples, but he is heavily based on his loadout, and which ones you want in play together.  If you get it all out there is a lot to keep track of.
So he's complex, but more because of the amount of stuff you can do each turn, rather than trying to pull complex shenanigans like Adept.
